title: Values and data types
learningObjectives: Explain values and data types and write predictable JavaScript code using the concept.

understand.concept: JavaScript values have types. Primitive types include string, number, bigint, boolean, undefined, symbol, and null. Objects are non-primitive values and include arrays, functions, and many built-in structures. Variables hold references to values rather than containing typed declarations in the way some languages do.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding types helps prevent invalid operations and unexpected conversions. JavaScript is dynamically typed: a variable can later refer to a value of a different type.
understand.analogy: A value has a kind, like a number or a piece of text; operations should make sense for the kind of value being used.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript values, scope, and runtime behaviour follow the language specification.

explain.narrative: The console reports string, number, boolean, and object for these values. Note that typeof null is a historical JavaScript quirk that reports object.

examples.code: <script>const learner='Asha';const lessons=4;const active=true;const profile={name:learner,lessons,active};console.log(typeof learner,typeof lessons,typeof active,typeof profile);</script>
examples.explanation: The console reports string, number, boolean, and object for these values. Note that typeof null is a historical JavaScript quirk that reports object.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page or developer console shows the values and behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Create one example for each primitive type and one object. Use typeof and explain any surprising result.
practise.independentTask: Write a short program that uses the concept in a realistic learning-app example. Inspect values and errors in the console.
hints: Prefer const unless reassignment is required.
Do not expose private data in console output.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Values and data types</title></head><body>
<script>const learner='Asha';const lessons=4;const active=true;const profile={name:learner,lessons,active};console.log(typeof learner,typeof lessons,typeof active,typeof profile);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which JavaScript type represents true or false values?
questions.explanation: boolean has the two logical values true and false.

questions.prompt: What should a learner do when a JavaScript value behaves unexpectedly?
options: Assume every variable has a fixed type
questions.explanation: Inspecting type and value helps identify unexpected coercion or operations.
